headline: Home Depot beat lowered Q4 EPS estimates with US comps +0.3%; guided FY2026 comps flat to +2% amid soft housing.
guidance_note: FY2026: sales +2.5-4.5%, comps ~flat to +2%, gross margin ~33.1%, ~15 new stores, adj EPS ~flat to +4% vs $14.69.
key_messages: US comps +0.3% (total +0.4%); sales fell 3.8% only because the prior-year quarter had a 14th week (~$2.5bn).
Big-ticket (>$1,000) transactions +1.3%, led by plumbing, electrical and power rather than appliances and remodels.
Decker: adjusting for storms, underlying demand was relatively stable through the year amid ongoing softness.
Pro outpaced DIY in Q4; company cites share gains from Pro investments.
Adj EPS $2.72 vs $3.13 a year earlier, but above consensus (~$2.53).

consumer.big_ticket: Transactions over $1,000 +1.3%, driven by repair-type categories (plumbing, electrical, power) rather than appliances and discretionary remodeling.
consumer.pricing: Management discussed tariff exposure in Q&A, citing roughly ~3% SKU-level price impact; average ticket up modestly.

macro_read: Home improvement spending is flat in real terms: needs-based repairs continue, but a frozen housing market keeps discretionary projects deferred.

sources.label: Newsquawk: HD Q4 adj EPS $2.72 vs exp $2.53
